# sandbox

Sandbox is a session-scoped service between you and the world you are not
trusted with directly. It does three things:

- Decisions. You post a question with a fixed set of answers and the files
  that make it concrete; the person answers in a browser at {{PUBLIC_URL}}
  and you read the answer here. Choosing a poster, approving a theme,
  comparing a replacement, confirming a change, asking a question.
- Upstreams. Your requests to configured APIs ({{UPSTREAMS}}) go through
  the sandbox, which injects the credential and enforces an allow list.
  You never need or see a key.
- Nothing kept. A reset or a container restart forgets every decision and
  deletes every file. Copy anything worth keeping into the repository.

## Loop

1. Prepare everything you can decide-ready (candidates encoded, files
   named, YAML written).
2. Post one decision per question. Post them all before waiting.
3. Tell the person in chat what is waiting at {{PUBLIC_URL}}.
4. Long-poll /answers. Act on each answer as it arrives.
5. A verdict of "changes" or "none" asks for another attempt: post a new
   decision with "supersedes" set to the old id, using the note.
6. Stop when every decision you posted has an answer that is not
   "changes" or "none". Then do what was approved and reset.

If /answers returns [] a few times in a row, ask in chat instead of
waiting further.

## Types

    choose    2 or more options; they pick min..max of them (default 1),
              or "none" with a note if none is right
    approve   1 option; "accept", "changes" or "reject"
    compare   options "current" and "new"; "new", "current" or "changes"
    confirm   no options; "yes" or "no"
    ask       no options; a free-text answer arrives in "note"

Every answer may carry a note. Read it.

## Posting a decision

Multipart: a "spec" field with the JSON, plus one part per file named in
the spec. Files are matched by filename; names must be plain (no
directories). A decision with no files can be bare JSON.

    curl -s -X POST {{PUBLIC_URL}}/decisions \
      -F 'spec={
        "title": "Poster for The Good, the Bad and the Ugly (1966)",
        "prompt": "Three TMDb candidates, encoded and cropped to 2:3. Current poster attached.",
        "type": "choose",
        "options": [
          {"id": "a", "label": "Italian 1966 one-sheet", "file": "a.jpg"},
          {"id": "b", "label": "Criterion-style",        "file": "b.jpg"},
          {"id": "c", "label": "Textless key art",       "file": "c.jpg"}
        ],
        "attachments": [{"name": "current poster", "file": "current.jpg"}]
      }' \
      -F file=@a.jpg -F file=@b.jpg -F file=@c.jpg -F file=@current.jpg

    curl -s -X POST {{PUBLIC_URL}}/decisions \
      -F 'spec={"title":"Replace the background?","type":"compare",
           "options":[{"id":"current","file":"old.jpg"},{"id":"new","file":"new.jpg"}]}' \
      -F file=@old.jpg -F file=@new.jpg

    curl -s -X POST {{PUBLIC_URL}}/decisions \
      -F 'spec={"title":"Theme for For a Few Dollars More (1965)","type":"approve",
           "prompt":"Main title, 60 s, 2 s fade.",
           "options":[{"id":"theme","file":"theme.mp3"}]}' \
      -F file=@theme.mp3

    curl -s -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' {{PUBLIC_URL}}/decisions \
      -d '{"title":"Remove the three Agregarr collections?","type":"confirm"}'

    curl -s -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' {{PUBLIC_URL}}/decisions \
      -d '{"title":"Which TVDb id is Agent Carter (2015)?","type":"ask",
           "prompt":"281485 (2015 series) or 362472 (2018 short)?"}'

Spec fields:

    title        required
    prompt       what you did and what you want; shown above the options
    type         choose | approve | compare | confirm | ask
    options      [{id, label?, file?}]   what can be picked
    attachments  [{name?, file}]         context shown but not pickable
    min, max     choose only; how many to pick (default 1 and 1)
    none         choose only; whether "none" is allowed (default true)
    supersedes   id of the decision this one revises

Images, audio, video and text (YAML, JSON, Markdown, plain) are shown
inline; anything else is a download link. Images show their dimensions,
aspect ratio and size, so put the encoded final file in the option, not a
draft. Per-file limit is 50 MB by default.

The response is the decision as JSON with its "id" (d1, d2, ...).

## Reading answers

    curl -s "{{PUBLIC_URL}}/answers?since=0&wait=300"

Returns every answer with a sequence number after "since", oldest first.
With "wait", the request blocks until at least one such answer exists or
the seconds elapse (max 300), then returns [] if nothing came. Pass the
last "seq" you saw as the next "since"; nothing is missed or repeated.

    [{"decision":"d1","seq":7,"verdict":"selected","selected":["b"],
      "note":"the blue one","at":"..."}]

Verdicts by type: choose -> selected (with "selected" ids) or none;
approve -> accept, changes, reject; compare -> new, current, changes;
confirm -> yes, no; ask -> answered (the text is in "note").

    GET {{PUBLIC_URL}}/decisions        every decision with its answer, newest first
    GET {{PUBLIC_URL}}/decisions/<id>   one decision

## Upstreams

Each upstream allows only the requests listed for it; anything else is
403 with the allowed list in the body. Check before guessing:

    curl -s {{PUBLIC_URL}}/upstreams      # {"tmdb": ["GET /3/movie/*", ...], ...}

    curl -s "{{PUBLIC_URL}}/tmdb/3/search/movie?query=A%20Fistful%20of%20Dollars&year=1964"
    curl -s "{{PUBLIC_URL}}/tmdb/3/movie/429/images?include_image_language=en,null"
    curl -s -H 'Accept: application/json' "{{PUBLIC_URL}}/plex/library/sections"

The path after /<upstream>/ is the upstream's own path and query, exactly
as its API documents them. Do not add a key or token; the server injects
the credential and drops any Authorization header you send. Plex answers
XML unless asked for JSON. TMDb image files live on
https://image.tmdb.org/t/p/original<file_path> and need no key.

## Housekeeping

    curl -s -X POST {{PUBLIC_URL}}/reset    # forget everything
    curl -s {{PUBLIC_URL}}/healthz
    curl -s {{PUBLIC_URL}}/version
